record.paper_title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems
record.original_question: For the phonon resolvent in Euclidean random matrices, how can one obtain a practical whole-spectrum approximation, ideally variational, when the one-loop method works only near the band edge and the action is too complicated for the variational computation currently known to the author?

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, the one loop result is already a good starting point to perform detailed comparisons with the numerical simulations. The disadvantage of this approach is that it works near band edge (ω = 0 at high ρ but is not suited for producing the whole spectrum. Due to the complication of the action it is not clear how to do a variational computation and the best it can be done at the present moment is a CPA-like approximation described in the next section.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N$ be $N$ points drawn independently and uniformly at random from a region of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with density $\rho$, and let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a fixed smooth, rapidly decaying pair potential. Define the Euclidean random matrix $M$ of size $Nd\times Nd$ in block form by
$$M_{ij}^{\alpha\beta}=\delta_{ij}\sum_{k\ne i}\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta f(x_i-x_k)-(1-\delta_{ij})\,\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta f(x_i-x_j),\qquad \alpha,\beta\in\{1,\dots,d\},$$
so that $M$ plays the role of the dynamical (Hessian) matrix governing harmonic phonon excitations of a topologically disordered solid. Let
$$G(z)=\frac{1}{Nd}\,\mathbb{E}\,\operatorname{Tr}(z-M)^{-1}$$
be the averaged resolvent (whose imaginary part on the real axis gives the vibrational density of states as a function of frequency $\omega$, with $z=\omega^2+i0^+$).

It is known that a one-loop expansion around the high-density saddle point of the field-theoretic representation of $G(z)$ provides a controlled approximation only near the low-frequency band edge $\omega\to 0$ at large $\rho$, while the effective action is too involved to admit a tractable Gaussian variational treatment.

Problem: Construct a practical analytic approximation scheme for $G(z)$ — ideally derivable from a variational principle on the field-theoretic action — that is accurate uniformly across the entire support of the spectrum of $M$ (not only near the band edge), and that improves systematically upon the CPA-type self-consistent approximation.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for variational whole-spectrum approximations of the phonon resolvent in Euclidean random matrices did not surface a definitive resolution. Subsequent work (e.g., on multi-space Euclidean random matrices and non-Hermitian Euclidean random matrix theory) has extended resolvent techniques and self-consistent equations, but no source clearly establishes a variational scheme accurate over the entire spectrum that supersedes the CPA-like approximation. The status is therefore inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Spectrum of multispace Euclidean random matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Resolvent computed using free probability and replica method in high-density regime.
status_evidence.claim: Later work extends resolvent methods for Euclidean random matrices but does not provide a variational whole-spectrum scheme.

status_evidence.title: On the Spectrum of Multi-Space Euclidean Random Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Additive superimposition of independent Euclidean random matrices; resolvent via free probability and replicas.
status_evidence.claim: Newer analyses focus on related but distinct setups, leaving the variational whole-spectrum question unaddressed.
